content:
What to pack for hiking Mt Kenya comes down to staying warm and dry from the wet forest to the freezing summit: broken-in waterproof boots, a base layer, fleece, insulated jacket and waterproof shell, two pairs of gloves, a warm hat, a headlamp, water bottles and a warm sleeping bag if your operator does not provide one.

Mt Kenya's trekking summit, Point Lenana, stands at 4,985 m, and a typical climb crosses four climate zones in four or five days. Pack too little and summit night is miserable or unsafe; pack too much and your porter bag goes over the limit. This checklist covers what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya, what goes in your daypack, what to leave at home and how to get ready.

Quick Facts

  • Trekking summit: Point Lenana, 4,985 m; the higher peaks Batian (5,199 m) and Nelion (5,188 m) need technical climbing skills and equipment
  • Typical trip: 4-5 days on the Sirimon, Naro Moru or Chogoria routes, often going up one route and down another
  • Climate zones: forest, bamboo, moorland and alpine, from mild and wet to below freezing
  • Summit night: starts at about 2:00-3:00am in sub-zero temperatures to reach Point Lenana around sunrise
  • Driest months: January-February and roughly July-September; the long rains run roughly March-May and the short rains roughly October-December
  • Packing system: what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya splits into a 25-35 litre daypack you carry, plus a duffel or large pack that porters carry if you use them

What Is the Complete List of What to Pack for Hiking Mt Kenya?

The complete list of what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya is a full layering system, waterproofs, warm accessories, sturdy boots, a headlamp, water and sun protection, plus sleeping gear if it is not provided. Everything else is a comfort extra.

Use the checklist below as your master list for what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya. Before you decide what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya, ask your climbing operator which items they provide, because many organised climbs include tents, cooking equipment and meals, and some include or hire out sleeping bags and mats.

How Do You Pack Clothing for Mt Kenya's Climate Zones?

Pack clothing for Mt Kenya as layers, not as one heavy outfit; layering is the heart of what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya. You walk in light layers through the warm, wet forest and add a fleece, insulated jacket and shell as you climb into the moorland and alpine zones.

Temperatures drop steadily as you gain height, which is why what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya covers such a wide range of conditions, and the weather on the mountain can switch from sun to mist and rain within an hour. Layers let you adjust quickly without getting soaked in sweat or rain. Our guide to layering for cold weather hikes explains how each layer works.

ZoneApprox. altitudeWhat you wear
Forest and bamboo2,000-3,000 mLight base layer, trekking trousers, rain jacket ready
Moorland3,000-3,800 mBase layer, fleece, shell jacket and rain pants in the rain, gaiters

Summit push to Point Lenana4,300-4,985 mBase layer, thermal leggings, fleece, insulated jacket, shell, thick gloves, balaclava

What should you wear on summit night?

On summit night, wear a base layer top and thermal leggings, trekking trousers, a fleece, an insulated jacket and a waterproof shell, plus liner gloves under insulated gloves and a warm hat or balaclava. Start slightly cool, because you warm up quickly once you are moving.

A spare pair of warm gloves belongs on any list of what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya. Keep them and your headlamp batteries in an inside pocket, where body heat stops the cold from draining them. Warm feet start with good socks, such as merino wool hiking socks, and cold hands are best protected by Thinsulate waterproof hiking gloves over a thin liner pair.

What Goes in Your Daypack and What Goes in the Porter Bag?

Your daypack holds everything you need while walking: water, snacks, rain gear, a warm layer, sun protection, a headlamp and personal medication. The porter bag holds your sleeping kit, spare clothes and camp items, and you will not see it until camp.

When you split what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya into two bags, remember that porters usually walk at a different pace from you, so never put anything you might need during the day in the porter bag. Operators set their own weight limit for porter bags, so ask yours and weigh your bag at home in Nairobi before you leave.

What to pack for hiking Mt Kenya in your daypack

  1. 2-3 litres of water in bottles or a bladder.
  2. Rain jacket and rain pants, packed at the top.
  3. Fleece or light insulated jacket for rest stops.
  4. Sun hat, sunglasses, sunscreen and lip balm.
  5. Headlamp, snacks, toilet paper and hand sanitiser.
  6. Phone, a small power bank and any personal medication.

What to pack for hiking Mt Kenya in the porter bag

Pack your sleeping bag, spare base layer, thermal leggings, spare socks, camp shoes, toiletries and charging cables in the porter bag, all inside dry bags. Line the bag with a strong bin liner, because porter bags are often carried through rain and mud on the lower slopes.

Good boots matter more than anything else in what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya. A waterproof pair such as the Quechua waterproof hiking boot paired with waterproof leg gaiters handles the boggy moorland sections. Our guide on where to buy hiking boots in Nairobi explains how to get the fit right.

What Should You Not Pack for Mt Kenya?

Do not pack cotton jeans, cotton hoodies, brand-new untested boots or single-use plastic bags for Mt Kenya. Cotton stays wet and cold, new boots cause blisters, and Kenya has banned single-use plastics in protected areas such as national parks and forests.

Knowing what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya also means knowing what to leave out. Leave heavy extras such as large toiletry bottles, several changes of town clothes and hardback books at your hotel or in Nairobi. Every extra kilogram counts against the porter limit, or on your own back if you carry your pack. If you are not sure about an item, ask whether you would use it every day; if not, it probably stays behind.

A rubbish bag belongs on your list of what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya too, so you can carry out wrappers and used batteries. Keeping the mountain clean protects the Mt Kenya National Park, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Pro Tips: Packing for Mt Kenya

  • Dry bags: pack your sleeping bag and insulated jacket in waterproof bags, even in the dry season
  • Test everything: wear your full summit layering system on a cold early-morning hike near Nairobi first
  • Keep power warm: carry batteries and your phone in an inside pocket on summit night
  • One dry set: always keep one base layer and one pair of socks dry for sleeping
  • Snacks: pack foods you enjoy, because appetite often drops at altitude
  • Label bags: mark your porter bag clearly so it is easy to find at busy camps

How Do You Prepare Before Hiking Mt Kenya?

Prepare for Mt Kenya by breaking in your boots, testing every layer together, getting fit on day hikes around Nairobi, and checking park information and the weather. Start your preparation four to six weeks before the climb.

Once you know what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya, wear your boots and carry your loaded daypack on two or three practice hikes, such as the crater rim walk in our Mt Longonot hike guide, so problems show up close to home. If you are also thinking about Tanzania's highest mountain, our Kilimanjaro gear checklist shows how much of the same kit carries over.

Altitude affects everyone differently, so climb steadily, drink regularly and tell your guide early if you feel unwell. Check the route, gate and park details on the Kenya Wildlife Service Mt Kenya National Park page, and confirm current conservation fees with KWS before you travel. Frequently Asked Questions

How many layers do you need for Mt Kenya?

Mt Kenya climbers need four upper-body layers for summit night: a base layer, a fleece, an insulated down or synthetic jacket and a waterproof shell. On the legs, wear thermal leggings under trekking trousers, with rain pants on top in wind or rain. Lower on the mountain you will wear only one or two of these layers.

How heavy should my bag be for Mt Kenya?

The right bag weight for Mt Kenya depends on your operator, because each operator sets its own weight limit for porter bags. Ask before you decide what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya, and weigh your bag at home. Your daypack should stay light, usually water, snacks, rain gear, a warm layer and small essentials.

Do I need trekking poles for Mt Kenya?

Trekking poles are optional when you decide what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya, but many climbers find them very helpful. Poles reduce strain on the knees during the long descent, add balance on scree and boggy moorland, and help on the steep final climb to Point Lenana. Adjustable, collapsible poles pack easily in a porter bag.

Can I rent gear for climbing Mt Kenya?

Some Mt Kenya climbing operators hire out items such as sleeping bags, mats or jackets, so ask yours what is available and check its condition before the climb. Personal items such as boots, socks and base layers fit and perform better when they are your own, which is why most climbers buy them.

Is Mt Kenya cold at the top?

Mt Kenya is very cold at the top. Point Lenana is usually below freezing at dawn, and wind can make it feel much colder. Summit night starts in the dark at about 2:00-3:00am, so pack an insulated jacket, thermal leggings, two pairs of gloves and a balaclava or warm hat.

Final Thoughts

Knowing what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya means planning for both rain and frost: a full layering system, waterproofs, warm accessories, broken-in boots, a headlamp and plenty of water. Ask your operator what is provided, then pack the rest using the checklist above.
